name: Kitchen Line Positioning
summary: Kitchen line positioning is where you stand and how you hold yourself once you have reached the net: toes a few inches behind the line, paddle up, level with your partner. Almost every point above 3.0 is decided at this line, and the team that gets there and holds it wins most of them. Standing a foot too far back gives that advantage straight back.
whenToUse: You have arrived at the net behind a return or a drop and the rally is still alive.
The ball is being dinked and neither team has anything to attack.
Your partner has been pulled wide and the middle is opening up.
You are tempted to back up for a ball at your feet — this is the moment the position matters most.
howTo: Stand with your toes two or three inches behind the line, close enough to reach a dink without stepping in.
Hold the paddle up in front of your chest with the tip above your wrist.
Bend your knees and keep your weight forward on the balls of your feet.
Move when your partner moves, so the gap between you never opens.
Slide toward the sideline the ball is on and let the player closer to the middle cover it.
commonMistakes: Standing a foot or two behind the line, which turns every dink into an awkward half-volley.
Creeping onto or over the line, so any ball you volley is a fault.
Letting the paddle drop to your waist between shots — it cannot get back up in time for a speed-up.
Staying put while your partner slides across, which leaves a lane straight up the middle.
Backing up to play a low ball instead of bending your knees and resetting it from where you are.

drills.name: Toes on the line
drills.description: Your partner dinks at you from their kitchen. Play twenty balls without your feet leaving the line — no backing up, no stepping in. When you cannot reach a ball, bend instead of stepping.

drills.name: Move as one
drills.description: Two of you hold the kitchen line while a feeder sends the ball from side to side. Keep roughly eight feet between you and slide together — if the gap changes, the feeder stops and you reset.
